patients.summary: Hotel maintenance engineer with long-standing type 2 diabetes and hypertension who joins in 2020, adds hyperlipidemia, tophaceous gout and diabetic nephropathy, then stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma in 2024 treated with chemoradiation and durvalumab, and a Legionnaires' admission in 2025. Records arrive unevenly.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer his primary care here; his old doctor is cutting back hours and he wants someone he can reach by text. Works days as a maintenance engineer at a downtown hotel, prefers early slots. Has diabetes and blood pressure, on 4 meds. Membership info emailed. New patient visit booked 8/18 at 7:40. Release of records signed by email and sent to prior office.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

medications.drug: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 50 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet
aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
56M transferring care. Diabetes dx around 2007, always on metformin, never on insulin. BP dx about 6 yrs ago, on lisinopril and metoprolol since. Baby aspirin on his own for years, prior doc ok'd it. Takes ibuprofen now and then for aches after long shifts.

Doesn't check sugars at home much, maybe once a week fasting, 130s-150s. No polyuria, no vision change he's noticed, no foot numbness. No chest pain or DOE climbing the hotel stairwells, which he does all day.

Smoked about a pack a day for 30 years, quit in 2017 cold turkey. No alcohol, never really did. Married, two grown kids out of state.

Fam: father had DM2, HTN and an MI at 60. Mother HTN and high cholesterol. Paternal uncle with bad gout, lumps on his hands. Maternal grandfather lung cancer.

Meds: metformin 1000 bid, lisinopril 20, metoprolol succinate 50, ASA 81. NKDA.

Exam: well appearing, BMI ~29. BP as charted. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Feet: skin intact, monofilament normal bilaterally, DP pulses 2+. No edema.

A/P
1. DM2 - on metformin alone. A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today. Eye exam: none in years, gave him a list of local optometrists.
2. HTN - at goal-ish in office, continue lisinopril 20 + metoprolol.
3. Lipids - not on a statin. Checking a panel today; diabetic over 40 so I expect we'll be talking about one.
4. Former heavy smoker, quit 3 yrs ago - qualifies for annual low-dose CT. Will order at next visit once records are in.
5. HM: Tdap and PCV20 given today. Hep C and HIV screen once. Colonoscopy per old records, he thinks 2016 and normal.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, labs are back. A1c is a little over 7, which is reasonable. Kidney numbers and urine protein are normal, blood counts normal, hep C and HIV negative. The one that stands out is cholesterol: LDL (the bad one) is about 160 and HDL is low. With diabetes and your dad's heart attack, I'd recommend a statin like atorvastatin. It's cheap and well studied. Let me know what you think.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks doc. I'd rather not add another pill yet. My wife is already on me about the food. Can I try cutting the fried stuff and the vending machine at work for a few months and recheck?

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Fair enough, we'll recheck next summer. I'll keep bringing it up though.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
38 pages received from prior primary care office covering 2012-2020. Abstracted:
- Type 2 diabetes on problem list since 2007, metformin titrated to 1000 mg twice daily by 2010.
- Hypertension started on lisinopril 2014, metoprolol succinate added 2016.
- Screening colonoscopy 08/2016: normal to cecum, no polyps; repeat in 10 years.
- No lipid therapy on file. Tobacco cessation counseling 2016-2017.
- No eye exam reports in the packet.
Scanned under Media, routed to PCP.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before his shift for the seasonal flu shot. No fever today, no prior reactions. Quadrivalent given IM left deltoid, lot logged. Waited 15 min in lobby, fine. VIS given.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 3 mo f/u. Says he has cut out the soda and the vending machine chips, most days. Hotel occupancy is down with the pandemic so he's doing more projects, less overtime. No hypoglycemia sx. Taking all 4 meds.
O: BP and weight as charted. Lungs clear, RRR. No edema.
A/P:
- DM2: A1c today. Same metformin.
- HTN: fine, no change.
- Lipids: still prefers diet; recheck in summer.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast. Comparison: none.
Findings: Lungs are clear without nodules, consolidation or mass. No emphysema. Airways patent. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymphadenopathy. Heart size normal, no coronary artery calcification. No pleural effusion. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

Back to full schedule at the hotel, lots of overtime getting the pool and HVAC ready for reopening. Diet has slipped some. No sx.
Vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular. Feet ok.
DM2 - A1c drawn, likely mid 7s. Talked about adding a second agent if it keeps creeping; he'd rather tighten up first.
HTN - stable.
Lipids - asked again about a statin. Still a no for now, will recheck at physical.
Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 57 y/o.
Interval: busy summer at work, no illnesses. No chest pain, dyspnea, cough, GI or GU complaints. Mood good.
Meds unchanged: metformin 1000 bid, lisinopril 20, metoprolol succ 50, ASA 81. NKDA.
Social: former smoker (quit 2017), no EtOH.
ROS otherwise negative.
Exam: NAD. HEENT nl, TMs clear. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft NT. GU deferred. Skin no concerning lesions. Ext no edema. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses good, no calluses.
PHQ-9 1.
A/P
- DM2: A1c, CMP, urine microalb today.
- HTN: controlled.
- Hyperlipidemia: lipids repeated. Diet effort real but numbers likely unchanged; statin discussed a third time. He'd like to wait for the result.
- Lung screening: due Dec, annual LDCT ordered.
- Eye exam: still hasn't gone. Reminded.
- Colon: due 2026.
- Flu/COVID booster this autumn when available.
See in 6 months.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Imaging center called: pt cancelled his screening CT, says the hotel is short-staffed and he can't get a weekday off before the holidays. They closed the order on their end. Pt told to call us when he wants it rebooked.

orders.reason: cardiovascular risk assessment; diabetes, hyperlipidemia, father with MI at 60

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rebooked after missing Jan. Feels fine. Sugars he checks are 140s fasting. BP at the pharmacy kiosk 130s/80s.
Exam: BP as charted, lungs clear, RRR, no edema. Feet fine.

We went back over cholesterol. He says his father was 60 when he had his heart attack and he's 58 now, which is on his mind, but he still doesn't love the idea of a statin from me. Asked if a heart doctor could look at his whole picture. Reasonable - placed cardiology referral for risk assessment. Their office will draw a lipid panel and A1c before the visit, so not repeating today.

BMP today. Meds unchanged. Return after cardiology.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT CARDIOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 04/13/2022
Referring: primary care physician
Reason: cardiovascular risk evaluation

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Desrosiers, a 58-year-old hotel maintenance engineer with long-standing type 2 diabetes, hypertension and untreated hyperlipidemia. He comes in without complaints: no chest discomfort, exertional dyspnea, palpitations, presyncope or claudication, despite a physically demanding job.

Risk factors: diabetes since about 2007; hypertension; former smoker, quit five years ago; no alcohol. Father had a myocardial infarction at 60.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: BMI 29. BP 135/85, HR 78 and regular. JVP not elevated. Carotids without bruit. S1 S2 normal, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No peripheral edema; distal pulses intact. Overall unremarkable.

Labs (04/06/2022): total cholesterol 210, HDL 35, LDL 160, triglycerides 150 mg/dL. HbA1c 7.2%.

Impression: Primary prevention in a diabetic man with low HDL, LDL 160 and a paternal history of MI at 60. His estimated 10-year ASCVD risk by the pooled cohort equations is in the elevated range, and diabetes alone puts him in statin territory.

Recommendations:
1. Start atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Prescription sent. Repeat lipids and hepatic panel in 6-8 weeks through your office.
2. Continue current antihypertensives; home goal under 130/80.
3. No ischemic testing indicated in the absence of symptoms.
4. Continue aspirin per your discretion.
Happy to see him again as needed.

Outpatient cardiology

documents.title: cardiology letter
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Mark, we received your cardiology letter. Atorvastatin 40 mg daily has been added to your medication list here. Dr. would like lipids and liver tests in about 6-8 weeks; your follow-up on 6/7 works for that.

documents.title: RE: cardiology letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok. Started it Saturday. Figured if the heart guy says so too I'll stop fighting it.

orders.reason: right hand nodules and swelling; recurrent first-toe attacks

documents.title: Hand pain / lipids
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 2 months of right hand aching and puffiness, stiffest when he first gets up and loosens as he works. Hurts gripping a wrench. Also, when asked about other joints, admits the big toe on the right has "flared" several times over the last couple of years - comes on overnight, burning, can't stand a sheet on it, he takes ibuprofen and it's gone within a week. Never mentioned it because it always went away. Uncle had gout with lumps on his fingers. No fever, no injury. Statin going fine, no muscle aches.

O: Vitals as charted. Right hand: firm, irregular nodules over several DIP joints, asymmetric, not warm today; grip mildly reduced by pain. Left hand unremarkable. Right 1st MTP not inflamed today. Heart/lungs ok.

A/P
1. Right hand nodules + history of podagra-type attacks: suspect chronic gout with tophi. Referring to rheumatology for evaluation (and possible aspiration). Holding off on starting urate lowering myself so they can see it fresh.
2. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40 x 7 wks: lipids and LFTs today.
3. DM2/HTN: unchanged; A1c at next visit.

documents.title: Lipids on statin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark - the atorvastatin is doing its job. LDL down from 160 to about 80, liver tests normal. Keep it going. Rheumatology should call you to schedule.

events.reason: right hand swelling, recurrent first MTP attacks

conditions.label: Chronic gout, unspecified, with tophus (tophi)
conditions.note: tophaceous gout, right hand DIP tophi, right first MTP attacks

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY NEW CONSULT
Visit date: 07/11/2022

HPI: 58M referred for three months of progressive right hand pain and swelling. Morning-predominant, improves once he is up and working. Separately, recurrent attacks in the right great toe over about two years, which he calls excruciating and burning, each lasting under a week with ibuprofen. No trauma, no fevers.

PMH: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia. Meds: metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.
FH: paternal uncle with tophaceous gout. SH: former smoker, no alcohol, hotel maintenance work.

Exam: Firm asymmetric nodules at the right 2nd-4th DIP joints, chalky in appearance under the skin, non-tender. Right first MTP swollen and tender to palpation without overlying cellulitis. Wrists, MCPs, PIPs, elbows, knees and ankles otherwise without synovitis. No nodules on the ears or elbows.

Labs today: uric acid 9.2 mg/dL; ESR 30 mm/hr; CRP 2.5 mg/dL. CBC within normal limits. Creatinine and BUN within normal limits.

Assessment: Tophaceous gout with hand tophi and recurrent podagra, hyperuricemia.

Plan:
- Allopurinol 300 mg daily started; target uric acid below 6.
- Uric acid with his PCP labs in 2-3 months.
- Low-purine, no-sugary-drinks handout.
- Return here as needed.

Outpatient rheumatology

documents.title: Fill history review
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pre-visit chart prep: pharmacy fill history shows allopurinol 300 mg daily filled 7/12 and 8/8, prescriber rheumatology. No rheum consult letter in chart yet. Added allopurinol to med list as reported by fill. Faxed request to rheumatology office for the 7/11 note.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Chronic disease follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen by rheumatology in July for the hand - tophaceous gout, put on allopurinol 300. Toe quiet since. Letter came in last month.

BP: brought his log. Readings this past year mostly 138-144 over 82-90. Admits the salt hasn't really changed - deli sandwiches at work, canned soup. Otherwise feels well, no complaints.

Office BP 148/86, pulse 76. Exam unremarkable - heart, lungs, abdomen, no edema, feet intact.

UA in office: protein 1+, glucose negative. Sent BMP, urine microalb, A1c, uric acid.

A/P
1. HTN above goal for a diabetic. Options: up lisinopril to 40 or add a third agent. He brought up a flyer from the hotel break room - a research group in the area enrolling people with high BP for a blinded drug study - and would rather do that than change his meds right now. I'm ok with that if they take him; gave him their number and he'll sign the release so they can get our notes. Keep working on sodium; gave low-sodium handout.
2. DM2 with proteinuria - will see what the ratio shows.
3. Gout on allopurinol - uric acid today.
4. Lipids at goal on atorvastatin.
RTC 6 months, sooner if trial wants anything.

documents.title: Kidney results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mark, results from Tuesday. Creatinine 1.1, which is normal filtering. But the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio is 120 (normal is under 30), which fits with the 1+ protein on the dipstick. In someone with diabetes for 15 years, this is diabetic kidney disease, early stage. It's one more reason to get the BP down. Two things: keep the lisinopril, it protects the kidneys; and please stop the ibuprofen for aches - Tylenol is safer for you now. Uric acid came down nicely to the low 6s on allopurinol.

documents.title: RE: Kidney results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Didn't know that about the advil. Ok. The study people called, I have a screening visit in early November.

documents.title: Seasonal vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (L) and bivalent Pfizer (R) given, no issues. BP not checked today per pt, in a hurry.

documents.title: Research site enrollment letter
documents.author: research coordinator
documents.body:
To the primary care physician of Mark Desrosiers:

Your patient was enrolled on 11/08/2022 in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of an investigational antihypertensive agent, taken once daily in addition to his current regimen. He will be seen at our site every 6-8 weeks for BP, labs and safety review through approximately August 2023. He should continue all of his usual medications. Please let us know before any change to his blood pressure medicines, and call our 24-hour line (978-555-0142) with any concerns. Study medication should be documented as "investigational product (blinded)".

Clinical research coordinator

documents.title: study update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI had my second visit at the blood pressure study. They said the numbers are coming down. Still taking everything else the same. They gave me a card to carry that says I'm in a study.

documents.title: RE: study update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks Mark, noted in your chart. Keep that card in your wallet.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail order renewal request: metformin 1000 bid, lisinopril 20, metoprolol succ 50, atorvastatin 40. All active, last visit 9/22. Sent 90-day x3. Allopurinol is written by rheum, pt says they renewed it.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: type 2 diabetes with diabetic kidney disease, A1c rising

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six months since I last saw him. Diabetes, HTN, lipids, gout all reviewed.

In the BP study since November, visits at the research site every couple of months. Taking metoprolol, lisinopril and the study capsule (blinded) every day. Their readings and his home cuff are now in the 120s/70s. No dizziness. No new symptoms of any kind. No gout attacks.

He wanted to know how they decide who gets the real drug - whether the study nurse knows, and if he can find out. Explained randomization: a computer assigns each person to drug or placebo by chance so the groups are comparable, and in a double-blind study neither he nor the site staff know which he has until the study is unblinded. He can ask the site whether they'll tell participants afterward; many do. He seemed satisfied.

Exam: BP as charted, HR regular. Heart, lungs, abdomen unremarkable. No edema. Feet intact.

A/P
- HTN: controlled on current regimen + study product. No changes during the study.
- DM2 with diabetic kidney disease: A1c, BMP today. Has been drifting up. Referring to endocrinology - likely a second agent with renal benefit; would like their input given the kidneys.
- Gout: quiet, uric acid today.
- Lipids: on atorvastatin.
RTC after study ends / late summer physical.

documents.title: Records request from research site
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Research coordinator called for copies of last two office notes and recent BMP for study safety review. Release on file from November. Faxed 9/27/22 and 3/31/23 notes with labs.

documents.title: Research site completion letter
documents.author: research coordinator
documents.body:
Mr. Desrosiers completed his final study visit on 08/22/2023 and has stopped the investigational product. There were no study-related adverse events. He resumes routine blood pressure care with your office on his prior regimen. Treatment assignment will be shared with participants after database lock. Thank you for your support of the study.

Clinical research coordinator

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
59M, physical.
Study ended last week; off the study product, back on just lisinopril 20 and metoprolol 50 for BP. Home readings already back up to low-mid 140s. Feels well. A little more tired at the end of the day than he used to be, chalks it up to the heat in the mechanical rooms. Endocrinology appt is in October (wait list).
No chest pain, SOB, cough. No gout flares. Eating out less.
Meds: metformin 1000 bid, lisinopril 20, metoprolol succ 50, atorvastatin 40, allopurinol 300, ASA 81. NKDA.
Exam: BP as charted. NAD. Eyes - pupils equal, no fundoscopic exam today. Neck no nodes. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd benign. No edema. Feet: sensation intact to filament, DP/PT palpable. Right hand DIP tophi unchanged, nontender. Skin ok.
PHQ-9: 3.
A/P
- HTN: back above goal off study drug. Will revisit after endo/labs; continue current.
- DM2/DKD: labs today, endo in Oct.
- Lipids, gout: labs.
- Eye exam: still none on file - pushed again.
- Flu/COVID at a nurse visit in Oct.
- Colonoscopy due 2026.

events.reason: diabetic nephropathy follow-up; fatigue and frothy urine

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with proliferative diabetic retinopathy without macular edema, bilateral

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY CLINIC NOTE - 10/05/2023
Referred by PCP for type 2 diabetes with diabetic nephropathy.

Subjective: 60-year-old man, diabetes ~16 years, nephropathy recognized last year. Over the past few months he has noticed more fatigue and that his urine has been foamy. Says he keeps to a strict diet now. No polyuria/polydipsia, no hypoglycemia.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily; also lisinopril 20 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, allopurinol 300 mg. NKDA.

Objective: BP 145/90. Mild pitting edema of both lower legs. Dilated fundus exam: neovascularization in both eyes consistent with proliferative diabetic retinopathy; no macular thickening appreciated. Feet: sensation intact.
Labs today: creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, BUN 24 mg/dL. Urinalysis 2+ protein. Urine albumin/creatinine 400 mg/g.

Assessment:
1. Type 2 diabetes with diabetic nephropathy, albuminuria now 400 mg/g with rising creatinine and new edema.
2. Proliferative diabetic retinopathy, both eyes, found today. He has not had an eye exam in many years.
3. Hypertension above goal.

Plan:
- Urgent referral to retina for evaluation and treatment.
- Referral to nephrology given the trajectory.
- Continue metformin for now. Will discuss additional agents at follow-up once nephrology has weighed in.
- BP management with PCP.

Outpatient endocrinology

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu and 2023-24 COVID given. Pt mentioned endocrinology found "bleeding vessels" in his eyes and he sees a retina doctor next month; endo letter is in chart. Flagged to PCP.

documents.title: Retina consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
RETINA CONSULTATION 11/08/2023
Referred by endocrinology.
Visual acuity: correctable to near-normal OU. IOP normal OU.
Anterior segment: unremarkable OU.
Dilated fundus: neovascularization of the disc and elsewhere OU; no vitreous hemorrhage; no tractional detachment. OCT: no center-involving macular edema OU.
Impression: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy, both eyes, without macular edema.
Plan: Panretinal photocoagulation, right eye first then left about one month later. Glucose and BP control discussed. Will update.

Retina service

documents.title: eye laser
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Retina doctor wants to do laser on both eyes, one at a time, starting next week. Do I need to stop the aspirin? Can I drive after?

documents.title: RE: eye laser
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No need to stop the baby aspirin for retinal laser - the retina office will tell you if they feel differently. Your vision will be blurry and light-sensitive for a few hours, so have your wife drive you that day. Glad you're getting it done.

documents.title: Retina procedure letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Re: Mark Desrosiers
Panretinal photocoagulation completed: right eye 12/06/2023, left eye 01/10/2024, both in clinic under topical anesthesia, tolerated well. Diagnosis: proliferative diabetic retinopathy OU without macular edema. Return in 6 months for repeat exam and OCT, sooner for any sudden floaters or loss of vision.

Retina service

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Comparison: none. There is a mass-like opacity in the right lower lobe. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contour not well assessed on radiograph. Osseous structures intact.
reports.conclusion: Right lower lobe mass-like opacity in a former smoker. CT chest recommended.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

orders.reason: right lower lobe opacity on chest x-ray, former smoker, weight loss

documents.title: Cough / weight loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Cough about 3 weeks, mostly dry, some days a little clear phlegm, not getting better. No fever, no blood. Not short of breath on the job. Clothes looser - he weighed 89 at endo in the fall, 84 today, not trying. Appetite "meh".
Also: saw nephrology for the first time in January. Per pt they said kidney function is reduced but stable and to keep his medicines as they are and return in the fall. No letter here yet. Laser to both eyes done Dec and Jan, letter received.

O: Afebrile, sat as charted. Diminished breath sounds at the right base, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular. No nodes in neck or supraclavicular area. Trace ankle edema, same as fall.
CXR (in-house read): mass-like opacity right lower lobe.

A/P
- RLL opacity with cough and 5 kg unintended loss in a 30 pack-year former smoker. Concerned for malignancy. CT chest with contrast ordered urgently; BMP today to confirm kidney function is ok for contrast, hydrate. Called pt with the x-ray result before he left.
- Requested January nephrology note.
Will call with CT.

reports.text:
CT chest with IV contrast. Comparison: chest radiograph 02/07/2024 and low-dose CT 12/08/2020.
Lungs: A 4.0 cm solid mass in the right lower lobe, new since 2020. No other pulmonary nodules. No consolidation.
Mediastinum: Enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes in the right paratracheal, subcarinal and left paratracheal stations. Heart normal in size. No pericardial effusion.
Pleura: No effusion.
Upper abdomen: Adrenal glands and liver unremarkable on the included images.
Bones: No suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: 4 cm right lower lobe mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy, highly suspicious for primary lung cancer. Tissue sampling and PET-CT staging recommended.

orders.order: MRI brain with and without contrast

orders.reason: suspected lung cancer with mediastinal nodes

documents.title: CT result discussed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Mark (wife on speaker) at 7 before his shift. Went over the CT: 4 cm mass in the lower right lung and enlarged lymph nodes in the middle of the chest; most likely a lung cancer, needs a biopsy to know for sure and what kind. He was quiet, then asked if it had spread. Told him the nodes in the chest are involved, we need a PET scan and brain MRI to see the rest. Orders in for PET-CT and MRI brain, referrals to thoracic surgery (for biopsy of the nodes) and oncology, both marked urgent. He can call or text me anytime. Will check in after biopsy.

reports.text:
FDG PET-CT from skull base to mid-thigh. Fasting glucose acceptable for imaging.
Chest: Intensely FDG-avid right lower lobe mass corresponding to the 4 cm CT lesion. FDG-avid mediastinal lymph nodes at right paratracheal (4R), subcarinal (7) and left paratracheal (4L) stations. No avid hilar node on the left. No pleural effusion.
Abdomen/pelvis: Physiologic uptake in liver, bowel and urinary tract. Adrenals without abnormal uptake.
Bones: No abnormal osseous uptake.
reports.conclusion: Avid right lower lobe primary with ipsilateral and contralateral mediastinal nodal disease. No distant metastasis.

reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after gadolinium. No enhancing lesion. No acute infarct, hemorrhage or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. Major flow voids preserved.

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
THORACIC ONCOLOGY - NEW PATIENT, 04/15/2024

Diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma of the right lower lobe, cT2a N3 M0, stage IIIB, diagnosed by mediastinoscopy 03/19/2024. No treatment to date.

HPI: 60-year-old man seen with his wife. Persistent cough since about mid-January and a 10 kg unintentional weight loss over three months. Also follows with endocrinology and nephrology for diabetic kidney disease, and rheumatology for tophaceous gout. He saw a news story about a phase III trial comparing a new targeted drug with standard chemotherapy and wants to know if he should join.

PMH: type 2 diabetes with nephropathy and proliferative retinopathy (laser both eyes), hypertension, hyperlipidemia, tophaceous gout.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg bid, lisinopril 20, metoprolol succinate 50, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, allopurinol 300. NKDA.
Social: 30 pack-years, quit 2017. No alcohol. Hotel maintenance engineer.
Family: maternal grandfather with lung cancer.

Exam: Appears cachectic. Decreased breath sounds at the right lower lobe. Heart regular. No supraclavicular or cervical nodes. Abdomen benign. Remainder unremarkable.

Labs today: Hb 12.5, WBC 7.0, platelets 250. Fasting glucose 160. AST 35, ALT 30. Creatinine as resulted, eGFR reviewed for carboplatin dosing.
Imaging reviewed: CT 02/13 with 4 cm RLL mass and mediastinal adenopathy; PET-CT 02/26 without distant disease; brain MRI 03/05 negative.

Molecular (addendum 04/10): no EGFR, ALK, ROS1 or KRAS alteration detected. PD-L1 tumor proportion score 30%.

Assessment and plan:
Unresectable stage IIIB NSCLC. We talked through the trial he asked about in detail - what phase III means, randomization, and the potential benefits (access to a new drug, close monitoring) and risks (unknown side effects, possibly receiving the standard arm anyway). That study requires a specific targetable mutation, and his tumor has none, so he would not be eligible. The standard of care for him is concurrent chemoradiation with curative intent, followed by a year of durvalumab consolidation if there is no progression.
- Concurrent weekly carboplatin (AUC 2) and paclitaxel (45 mg/m2) with thoracic radiation, 60 Gy in 30 fractions. Radiation oncology consult arranged.
- Port not needed for weekly regimen; peripheral access.
He and his wife agree. Target start early May.

Thoracic oncology

RADIATION ONCOLOGY TREATMENT SUMMARY
Patient: Mark Desrosiers
Diagnosis: NSCLC, adenocarcinoma, right lower lobe, cT2a N3 M0, stage IIIB

Treatment: 60 Gy in 30 fractions to the right lower lobe primary and involved mediastinal nodes, IMRT, 05/06/2024 - 06/14/2024. Completed without breaks.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PROVIDER NOTE - 09/26/2025

CC: fever, cough, short of breath

HPI: 62-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, diabetic nephropathy (CKD 3b) and stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma treated with chemoradiation and durvalumab (finished June). Five days of high fevers and cough bringing up thick yellow-green sputum, increasingly short of breath. For the last two days, loose stools and, per his wife, confusion - repeating questions, mixing up days. Works as a hotel maintenance engineer.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg bid, lisinopril 20, metoprolol succinate 50, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, allopurinol 300. NKDA.

Exam: T 39.2 C (102.5 F), BP 135/85, HR 102, RR 22. Ill-appearing, oriented to person and place only. Crackles at both bases. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. No meningismus.

Data: WBC 15.0 (80% neutrophils), Hb 13.5, platelets 250. Na 130. Creatinine 2.4 (baseline about 2.1). Liver enzymes mildly elevated (AST 68, ALT 54). CXR: patchy infiltrates both lower lobes. Urine antigen for Legionella sent, pending.

ED course: blood cultures, 1 L IV fluid, IV azithromycin started given the diarrhea, hyponatremia, confusion and transaminases. Metformin held.

Impression: Community-acquired pneumonia, bilateral lower lobes, with sepsis physiology; concern for Legionnaires' disease. Acute kidney injury on CKD. Hyponatremia.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

Emergency medicine

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 09/26/2025, discharged 10/01/2025

Principal diagnosis: Legionnaires' disease (Legionella pneumonia), bilateral lower lobes.
Secondary: acute kidney injury on CKD 3b, resolved to baseline; hyponatremia, resolved; type 2 diabetes; hypertension; stage IIIB NSCLC, in surveillance.

Course: Admitted from the ED febrile and confused with bilateral lower lobe infiltrates. Urinary antigen returned positive on 09/27. Treated with IV azithromycin and IV fluids. Fever broke on hospital day 2, when the diarrhea and confusion also cleared. Remained on room air. Sodium corrected with fluids to 136; creatinine improved from 2.4 to 2.0. Blood cultures negative. Metformin held during the stay and restarted the day of discharge; all other home medicines continued. Case reported to the local board of health as required.

Discharge medications: azithromycin 500 mg by mouth daily for 5 more days (10 days total); otherwise home regimen unchanged.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with BMP. Oncology as scheduled; next surveillance CT will also document clearance of the infiltrates.

Hospital medicine

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
62M annual exam, delayed from August.
Interval: Legionnaires' admission 9/26-10/1, fully recovered; discharge summary received 10/28. Surveillance CT 11/12 clear. Done with durvalumab since June. Working full time. Mood ok - "more grateful than anything." PHQ-9 4.
Meds: metformin 1000 bid, lisinopril 20, metoprolol succ 50, atorvastatin 40, allopurinol 300, ASA 81. NKDA.
ROS: foamy urine and ankle swelling unchanged. No chest pain, no dyspnea, cough resolved. No gout attacks.
Exam: BP as charted. NAD. Neck no nodes. Heart regular. Lungs: slightly decreased R base (radiation). Abd benign. bilateral ankle edema. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses palpable, no ulcers. Right hand tophi unchanged. Supraclavicular areas clear.

A/P
1. DM2 with DKD, A1c was over 9 in February with no change since (recheck today), eGFR mid-30s. He's ready now, as we planned in February. Metformin dose too high for this eGFR - reducing to 500 mg twice daily. Adding empagliflozin 10 mg daily, for both the kidneys and sugar. Counseled: genital hygiene, hold on sick days (vomiting, not eating, like in September), expect more urination. Insurance will likely need a PA.
2. CKD 3b A3 - BMP 4-6 weeks after starting empagliflozin. Nephrology due for their 6-month visit - he'll call them.
3. HTN above goal - continue for now; reassess once SGLT2 on board.
4. Gout, lipids - labs today.
5. Lung cancer surveillance with oncology, next CT Feb.
6. HM: flu/COVID done Oct. Colonoscopy due 2026 - discuss at next visit. RSV done 2024.
RTC 3 months.
